tasks.short: Develop social work knowledge through literature, research and training

steps.what: Locate current literature and relevant research or training opportunities

loop.purpose: Find potentially relevant sources for a stated learning question
loop.input: Worker-selected topic and retrievable source descriptions
loop.output: Candidate readings or courses with source links and relevance notes
loop.check: Worker opens sources and checks actual topic coverage, publication date, methods and training relevance
loop.stop: One refinement then manual search if support is weak
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters help discovery but relevance requires semantic reading

steps.what: Review literature critically and conduct social research
Attend seminars, workshops or classes and reflect on practice implications

tasks.design: Use native saved searches in {OTHER}, a research and training catalogue, before bounded source suggestions. The worker checks candidate sources and retains critical reading, research activity and training attendance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding relevant material can require repeated searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved search filters and source-linked suggestions can narrow discovery.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding methods and applying findings to practice.
tasks.human_edge: The worker evaluates evidence rather than treating a summary as learning.
tasks.altitude: Less discovery time; learning and research responsibility are unchanged.

evidence.claim: Source-linked retrieval can support discovery; no social-work learning time result is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary covers worker discovery, critical review, research and attendance. Shares are a workload mix; summaries do not replace any learning hours.

Worker states topic, intended learning goal and date or language constraints in retained s1 time. Publishers and course providers supply existing descriptions through unchanged publication work. Missing source access or uncertain references trigger manual search.
Test native saved searches first. No client information is needed.
research_questions: Does source discovery take less time after opening and checking every recommended source?

incremental.description: Maintain searches and examine retrieval errors

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90 gives10 gross minus3 upkeep net7. Low assumes only3 discovery hours removed;50 research and reading hours and30 training hours remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct community prevention and service-improvement programs

steps.what: Assess community needs and consult participants and service partners
Plan prevention or service-improvement programs and agree appropriate activities
Coordinate programme dates, resources and internal action reminders
Conduct programme activities and respond to participant needs

tasks.design: Keep community assessment, programme decisions and delivery human. Configure an internal activity schedule and reminders in {CALENDAR} to reduce repeated logistics messages without automating care or eligibility decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed activity details may be copied into multiple coordination messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared calendars can reuse agreed dates and responsibilities.
tasks.still_hard: Building trust and adapting prevention activities to real needs.
tasks.human_edge: The worker designs appropriate support with the community.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less logistics work; programme and care decisions are unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native calendars can reduce repeated coordination; the saving is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is worker programme planning and delivery, excluding other staff and participant labour.

Worker produces activity, owner, date constraints and resource needs in s2's35 hours. Partners supply availability through unchanged coordination; s3's9 remaining hours include capture, conflict checks and manual clarification. No structured participant risk or eligibility input is assumed.
Test native shared calendars first. Internal reminders carry logistics only, without client case detail.
unknowns: Coordination burden and partner calendar access
research_questions: Does a shared schedule reduce repeated messages after resolving availability conflicts?

incremental.description: Maintain schedule templates and reminder recipients

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94 gives6 gross minus2 upkeep net4. Low assumes2 hours repeated messaging removed;85 hours assessment, planning and delivery remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop social policy and advise community development

steps.what: Review policy evidence and community feedback relevant to the development question

loop.purpose: Organise supplied evidence and feedback into a sourced brief
loop.input: Worker-selected policy question, source passages and authorised feedback
loop.output: Draft brief separating evidence, opinions, gaps and conflicting accounts
loop.check: Worker checks each claim and attribution, verifies minority or conflicting views remain visible, and rejects unsupported causal conclusions
loop.stop: One revision then manual briefing if meaning is distorted
loop.why_not_simpler: Grouping and comparing narrative evidence requires semantic interpretation

steps.what: Develop policy options and judge consequences for the community
Advise policy partners and support community development discussions

tasks.design: Reuse briefing structures in {DOCS}, with a bounded assistant organising selected evidence and authorised feedback. The worker checks the complete brief, develops policy options and conducts all community and policy discussions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative evidence and feedback take time to organise.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bounded drafting can prepare a first-pass brief.
tasks.still_hard: Policy consequences, representation and competing interests need accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker preserves community voice and explains real tradeoffs.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass evidence organisation; policy authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Bring community experience into policy discussions
reach.learn: Distinguish evidence, interpretation and individual testimony

evidence.claim: Source-bounded briefing is plausible model capability; no measured social-policy result is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is worker evidence organisation, policy development and advice, excluding policy enactment and other participants' time.

Worker selects the policy question and supplied sources, checks authorisation and captures missing context within s1's18 remaining hours. Community partners produce original feedback through unchanged consultation work; no free structured sentiment or risk code is assumed. Unclear provenance means manual clarification or exclusion.
Test native briefing templates first. Use de-identified or authorised material and keep policy judgement human.
research_questions: Does brief drafting save time after checking attribution, omissions and conflicting views?

already_counted.description: Source selection, contextual clarification and complete brief review

incremental.description: Maintain briefing prompts and review recurring distortions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R88 gives12 gross minus4 upkeep net8. Low assumes4 briefing hours removed;70 policy judgement and discussion hours remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less discovery, evidence organisation and programme logistics; learning, policy judgement and community work remain human.
reach: Collaborate with community health workers on accessible programmes and evidence
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who organises information efficiently while retaining direct community participation and professional judgement.

job.title: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
